summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop system using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, covering all 12 subcommands in a single navigable app.
summary.outcome: A complete bubbletea TUI (`entire memory-loop tui`) was implemented with 4 tabs (Memories, Injection, History, Settings), lifecycle actions, search, add-memory form, and prompt tester. A post-build color fix changed the accent from cyan to orange (214) and made inactive tabs visible.

repo: The `memoryloop` package exposes `TransitionRecordLifecycle`, `AddManualRecord`, `PruneRecords`, `SelectRelevant`, and `SaveState` as the primary mutation surface for memory records.
The CLI uses `termstyle` for all color/style definitions; new TUI code should import styles from `memorylooptui/styles.go` rather than hardcoding lipgloss colors inline.
The `docs/superpowers/` directory is gitignored — spec and plan artifacts written there won't be committed.
ACCESSIBLE=1 mode is already handled at the cobra command level by falling back to plain-text `show` output, so the TUI itself doesn't need an accessible rendering path.
The project uses a worktree at `/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements` for this feature work.

code.finding: Accent color is ANSI 214 (orange). Inactive tab color must be 245 (light gray) not 8 (dark gray) — color 8 is invisible on dark terminals.

Table selected-row highlight had a hardcoded Color("6") (cyan) that bypassed the shared styles.go accent; must use the shared orange style. Detail pane is shown by default (showDetail initialized to true).
Had hardcoded cyan Color("6") for match result highlights; replaced with shared orange accent from styles.go.
Had hardcoded cyan Color("6") for table highlights; replaced with shared orange accent from styles.go.

workflow: Subagent-driven development (one agent per task, sequential dispatch) works well for multi-file bubbletea packages where tabs are largely independent but share scaffolding.
Tasks 1-3 (styles, render helpers, root model) are tightly coupled and should be dispatched as a single implementer agent rather than split.
The brainstorm visual companion server does not persist between sessions — it must be restarted and HTML content re-written if the session ends.
A post-implementation code review agent reliably catches issues like rune-unsafe string truncation (should use lipgloss.Width), missing empty-state messages, and search mode key conflicts.
Committing incrementally per logical task (scaffold, fixes, remaining tabs) keeps the git history readable and makes partial review easier.

friction: The brainstorm visual companion server shut down between the design phase and the user's follow-up request to view mockups, requiring a full server restart and HTML re-render.

The initial implementation used hardcoded Color("6") (cyan) in three tab files instead of referencing the shared accent variable in styles.go, causing the accent color change to require grep-and-fix across multiple files.
Inactive tabs used color 8 (dark gray) which is invisible on dark terminals — not caught until the user shared screenshots after implementation.
Tasks 5-9 were not auto-committed by the subagents, leaving a large uncommitted diff that required a manual commit step after the fact.
The gomod lint error after dependency promotion appeared alarming but was a false alarm — caused by go.mod changes not yet committed.
open_items: History tab `R` key to trigger refresh is a placeholder — async refresh is not yet wired to an actual `memoryloop.Refresh` call with a spinner.
No unit or integration tests for the `memorylooptui` package — the plan explicitly deferred this to manual verification.
The visual mockup in the browser and the actual TUI rendering differ in some ways (noted by the user with screenshots) — a closer visual audit pass may be worthwhile.
The `prune` action (`D` key) was added during spec self-review but its UX flow (confirmation prompt) was not fully specified or implemented.
The add-memory form (Task 8) covers basic fields but scope selection and kind validation were noted as areas needing polish.
